title: Refinement Strategies for Any-Angle Package Routing with I/O Alignment Consideration
problem: Traditional packaging routers support only 90- and 135-degree angles; advanced packaging with increased I/O demands requires any-angle routing to explore larger solution space and reduce wirelength, but I/O alignment constraints complicate routing.
motivation: Advanced packaging technologies demand higher I/O density; any-angle routing enables superior solutions, but existing methods lack optimization for I/O alignment constraints in die-to-substrate connections.
method: Framework introduces accurate routing resource utilization estimation in global routing stage, concurrent access point adjustment to reduce total wirelength across all nets simultaneously, and dynamic programming-based method minimizing wire segments per net.
key_novelty: Any-angle routing framework with two-stage wire-length optimization strategies considering I/O alignment constraints.

metrics.ppa: Superior routing quality vs. global routing

limitations: No quantitative comparison metrics provided; evaluation limited to specific packaging technology; scalability to large systems unclear.
